title: U.S. Strikes Qeshm Island as Vance Says Iran Won’t Become ‘Forever War’
author: Chad de Guzman
body:
The U.S. and Iran exchanged attacks on Tuesday in the latest flare-up of the war that the Trump Administration promised would end after the U.S. midterms.

American warplanes hit an Iranian missile launch site on Qeshm Island in the crucial Strait of Hormuz waterway. An unnamed official speaking to CNN and other outlets called the strikes “self-defense” in response to alleged “aggression targeting American personnel and assets” by Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps.

Iran had earlier attempted an attack on American military targets in Bahrain, which is home to the US Navy's Fifth Fleet. But the U.S. Central Command, which has jurisdiction in the Middle East, announced on social media that the Iranian one-way attack drones “were intercepted without any damage to U.S. equipment or injury to American personnel.”

Ahmad Nafisi, deputy governor of Iran’s southern Hormozgan province, also told state media Tuesday that the attacks on Qeshm “caused no damage to residential, commercial, or infrastructural areas.”

Kuwait’s Armed Forces also announced early Wednesday morning that its air defenses were responding to “drone attacks.” Iran later took responsibility for attacks on Kuwait’s Ali Al Salem Air Base, which hosts U.S. forces.

The latest flare-up resembled other recent skirmishes around the Strait of Hormuz. Washington has so far held back from resuming major hostilities with Tehran. Still, in the lead-up and the immediate wake of the U.S. midterm elections, Qeshm Island has become a major flashpoint, involving so-called “limited” strikes. On the eve of the midterms, the U.S. carried out an attack on the island, and Trump confirmed more strikes on Nov. 6.

The Wall Street Journal reported on Nov. 2 that the U.S. had engaged in smaller-scale, unannounced strikes against Iran “for several weeks,” with unnamed officials describing them as defensive and preventative of an Iranian attack on commercial ships in the strait.

The latest strikes came despite talks between Iran and mediators Oman and Qatar. An imminent diplomatic agreement to end the war has seemed unlikely. The U.S. has maintained its blockade on Iranian ports to cut off its oil exports and damage the Middle East nation’s economy. President Donald Trump also previously warned that full combat operations could continue if Iran refuses to heed the U.S.’s demands.

“We don’t need a deal with Iran,” Trump posted on his platform Truth Social on Nov. 12. “Those days have long since passed. We’ve got their money, Hundreds of Billions of Dollars, and we’ve got their Strait!”

Not a ‘forever war’

Trump’s Vice President J.D. Vance said earlier this week that the Administration won’t let the conflict with Iran last and that it will wrap up long before they leave the White House in 2029.

“[Trump] is not going to let this become a forever war,” Vance told Fox News on Monday. “And the people who want it to become a forever war, they can attack me all they want to, because we signed up to not do this. We told the American people we would do no more forever wars.”

Vance, considered a possible contender for the 2028 presidential election, blamed the American public’s frustrations with the ongoing Iran war for the GOP’s massive losses to Democrats during the midterms. Vance had originally been tasked with leading peace negotiations with Iran, but Trump on Nov. 12 reassigned him to focus domestically on investigating fraud in Democratic-led jurisdictions.

The U.S. appears to maintain its military might in the region, according to analysis by the Institute for National Security Studies in Israel; a third American aircraft carrier—the U.S.S. Theodore Roosevelt—arrived in the Middle East on Nov. 15. And Trump has warned that escalation by Iran would be responded to by the U.S. In Manila on Tuesday, the President said in response to questions regarding Iran reportedly developing plans to deploy a “dirty bomb” in Washington: “If there is, they will pay a price the likes of which no country has ever paid before.”

Trump is expected to hold a trilateral summit on Thursday in China with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin, where the Iran war is on the agenda.
